predecessors.name: Saadi Sultanate
predecessors.text: The pashalik: Timbuktu, Gao and Djenné with their surroundings (the page names the three cities and no frontier)

successors.name: Massina Empire
successors.text: Timbuktu, the pashalik's capital, with its Niger port: a 120 km disc (the page gives no extent)

ledger.x: 1618: the Arma state of Timbuktu starts when Morocco lets go.
1833: Massina takes firm control of Timbuktu.

wars.name: Tuareg takeover of Gao and Timbuktu
wars.outcome: About 1770 the Tuareg took Gao; "in 1787 they entered Timbuktu and made the Pashalik their tributary".

certainty.note: The page names three cities, no frontier; three discs stand for them, and the extent of Arma power is unknown.
The Arma may have lost Timbuktu in 1737 (body of the page) and were a Tuareg tributary from 1787 and a Massina vassal from 1826/7; the shape is held to the infobox end.
